llm.summary: This skill has a coherent file-editing purpose, but its scripts can modify or restore arbitrary local files without enough path checks and its safety claims are overstated.

dimensions.detail: Local file access is expected for this purpose, but the authority is under-scoped: writable files outside the intended skill or project can be changed or copied into backup/state locations if supplied through artifacts or CLI arguments.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No install-time execution, remote payload retrieval, package hooks, or dependency installation steps were observed in the artifact files inspected.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions disclose file mutation, backups, and rollback, but they claim execute dry-run previews and rollback SHA-256 verification that the inspected code does not implement; the one-word trigger '回滚' is also broad for a file-restoring skill.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill creates persistent backups under the OpenClaw state tree and pre-rollback backups beside selected targets; this is purpose-aligned, but lack of path and integrity validation makes that persistence capable of preserving or restoring unintended file contents.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: Applying approved improvement candidates and rolling them back is coherent, but execute.py trusts candidate target_path and rollback.py trusts receipt, backup, and target paths without binding them to an approved project or original target.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only use this skill in a constrained workspace with trusted ranking, receipt, and backup artifacts, and avoid running rollback with --execute unless the source backup and destination target are verified manually. Do not rely on the documented execute dry-run preview or rollback hash verification until the implementation actually enforces them.
llm.findings:
[T05] unexpected: Accepted as a material concern: file mutation and rollback are expected, but unrestricted candidate, receipt, backup, and target paths create overbroad local overwrite authority.
[T09] unexpected: Accepted: SKILL.md documents SHA-256 rollback verification and hash-bearing rollback data, while the inspected execute and rollback scripts only store paths and check backup existence.
[TP4] unexpected: Partially accepted and downgraded from scanner framing: the package does include both execute and rollback scripts, but advertised dry-run preview, hash verification, and some output fields do not match the implementation.
[LP3] unexpected: Accepted as contextual support: the skill requests file-changing behavior but does not provide clear path containment or least-privilege boundaries in the manifest or runtime checks.
[SQP-1] unexpected: Accepted as a lower-weight concern: a generic rollback trigger can activate a file-restoring workflow in unrelated contexts unless the orchestrator requires explicit selection and inputs.
[SDI-1] unexpected: Accepted for the execute dry-run and rollback-description mismatch; action-name concerns are mostly documentation quality because the detailed action table lists the actual implemented names.
[SDI-4] unexpected: Accepted as documentation inconsistency: rollback help text conflicts with the actual --execute requirement and backup filename format, which can confuse operators.
[TR1] unexpected: Accepted as overlapping with SQP-1: the broad trigger is not malicious by itself but increases accidental invocation risk for a mutating workflow.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: mixed Chinese and English documentation is not a material security issue for this artifact.
